$comment: Ground truth for the false-positive number. D-8.
A mark is a PERSON'S judgement about one PUSHED EVENT, made by looking at it.
The `tag` is the event tag the run pushed - `aicap-<class>-<16 hex>` - which is
the same string the read-back matches on, so a mark attaches to the event that
actually left the process and not to a detection row that merely resembles it.
THE CLASS IS THE PROMPT. Since W2-2 a tag begins `aicap-alarm-` for an incident
the alarm prompt asked about and `aicap-camera_integrity-` for one the
camera_integrity prompt asked about. A mark names the class it judged, which is
how two classes are reviewed separately without two code paths.
An EMPTY `marks` list is valid and means NOT RUN. It does not mean zero false
positives: it means nobody looked. Those are different claims and only one of
them is ever available.
STATE AS OF THIS BUILD: the list is EMPTY, and that is the honest state rather
than an omission. W3-5 asks for real marks and the plan allows the alternative:
the full `false positives: NOT RUN: no human marked any event in
testdata/groundtruth.json` sentence, which `pocctl report` prints and which
`TestTheFalsePositiveSentenceIsNeverAZeroNobodyMeasured` asserts. No live camera
and no live XProtect instance were reachable when this was written, so there
were no pushed events for a person to judge. A number written here without a
person having looked at the footage would be the exact failure this file exists
to prevent.
HOW TO FILL IT: run `pocctl demo --live` or a `watch` run against a real camera,
copy the tags out of `pocctl audit ledger` (they are the `push_enqueued` rows),
open each event in Milestone XProtect Smart Client, and mark it. One entry per
event. `pocctl report` then prints `false positives: <fp>/<tp+fp> (precision N)`,
or names which events it could not find rather than counting them as true.
Two verdicts, and only two:
true_positive   the event is a real crossing of a real object
false_positive  the event is not - a traffic light at night, a shadow, a
reflection, a lamp post the model calls a car
This file is a REVIEW, not a measurement the machine made. Nothing in this
repository computes it, infers it, or estimates it.
